text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants (exact, whitespace/case, punctuation, changed quantity, added negation, removed negation, reordered, paraphrase) for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2023, the Harrowmere Family Links Service received 142 new referrals for children separated from their caregivers in Ostrava District. Caseworkers completed initial assessments for 128 of these children within seventy-two hours, which is 90 percent of all new cases. Family tracing was successful for 37 children, and each reunification was followed by at least two home visits. Placement in foster care remained a last resort; no child under three was placed in residential care during the period. However, the monitoring team found that 14 case files did not contain a signed consent form from the foster family. Staff turnover in the northern office was also high, with four of nine caseworkers leaving before September.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Tamsin Valley Cash for Food Programme covered 2,400 households across six sub-counties between March and May 2024. Monthly transfers of 45 dollars reached registered households on time in 83 percent of distribution cycles. Households receiving transfers reported eating two meals a day on average, compared with one and a half meals at baseline. The evaluators did not find evidence that transfers raised prices in local markets. Female-headed households spent a larger share of the transfer on food than male-headed households did. Mobile money delivery reduced travel costs for recipients, but 310 households still had no registered phone and collected cash at pay points. The team recommends that the programme should not expand to new areas until the registration backlog is cleared.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, with support from the Brightwater Justice Fund, the Kessane Paralegal Network trained 26 community paralegals in Lower Maro and Felt Hill. Together they held 418 outreach sessions in markets, churches and chiefs' courts, reaching an estimated 9,000 people. Paralegals handled 1,150 individual cases, most of them land disputes and unpaid wages. Around 62 percent of cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Paralegals never charged clients a fee, and no client was turned away because of where they lived. We were not able to open the planned office in Felt Hill, because the district council did not approve the lease until November. That delay meant that clients in the eastern villages travelled up to fifteen kilometres for help.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Little Acorns Playgroup Network aimed to open 40 community playgroups in Dunmore County by June 2024. As of this update, 34 playgroups are running, each meeting three mornings a week. Attendance averages eleven children per session, slightly above the target of ten. Volunteer facilitators have completed the five-day play-based learning course, and parents now lead songs and storytelling in most groups. Six planned sites have not opened, mainly because suitable buildings could not be found. The network has not yet received the second tranche of funding from the Holloway Trust, so toy kits for new groups are on hold. Management does not recommend lowering the target at this stage.

passages.source_passage: Explain that each savings group should have between 15 and 25 members who know and trust one another. Members buy shares at every weekly meeting, usually worth between 200 and 500 shillings each. Remind members that no one may buy more than five shares in a single meeting. The cash box must have three locks, and the three key holders must not be members of the management committee. Loans are repaid with a service charge, often 10 percent per month. The secretary records every loan in the ledger while the treasurer counts the cash aloud. You should never hold the cash box or the keys yourself, even if the group asks you to. At the end of the cycle, normally after twelve months, savings and profits are shared out.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation reviewed the Sankoré Hot Meals Initiative in 48 public primary schools across the Bénou and Kalfa regions of Toravie. Between October 2022 and June 2024, the programme served a daily lunch of rice, beans and fortified oil to approximately 19,500 pupils. Enrolment in participating schools rose by 12 percent, while comparison schools saw almost no change. Girls' attendance improved more than boys' attendance, particularly in the upper grades. Food deliveries were late in 9 of 21 months, and on those days cooks often served porridge instead. Parent committees supplied firewood and water, but they were not trained in basic food hygiene. The evaluation did not measure changes in children's height or weight.

passages.source_passage: Thanks to continued support from the Merrow Health Foundation, the Ubuntu Lane Home Care Project reached 1,320 clients living with HIV in Nkalo and Riverside wards during 2023. Our 85 community care workers made 14,600 home visits, checking medication supplies, wounds and nutrition. Viral load results were available for 870 clients, and 91 percent of them were virally suppressed. Care workers also referred 212 clients to clinics for tuberculosis screening. Stigma remains a serious barrier; several families asked that care workers not wear project T-shirts when visiting. No care worker received a stipend increase this year, and eleven left for paid jobs. We did not reach our target of enrolling 300 new clients, because two clinics stopped sharing referral lists in April.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the Saltmarsh Coast Early Warning Programme from January to June 2024. Sirens were installed in 22 of the 25 target villages along the Pellan shoreline, and all 22 passed their monthly sound tests. Village warning committees ran evacuation drills in 18 villages, with an average of 340 residents taking part in each drill. In Corrow and Vey, drills were not held because the access road flooded in March. SMS alerts reached 76 percent of registered phone numbers within ten minutes of being sent. Older residents said the text messages were harder to understand than the sirens, partly because they were written only in the national language. No evacuation was required during the period, so the full warning chain was not tested in a real event.

passages.source_passage: Kambura Camp hosts approximately 38,000 refugees, most of whom fled conflict in the neighbouring Velde Highlands after 2019. Women and children make up 71 percent of the camp population. Since 2021, the Tessaly Refugee Support Network has provided case management for survivors of violence, unaccompanied children and people with disabilities. Last year our six caseworkers opened 940 new cases, but the caseload per worker was more than double the recommended standard. Many survivors do not report incidents because they fear retaliation from community leaders. There is no safe shelter inside the camp, and the nearest one is four hours away by road. This proposal requests funding for three additional caseworkers and a confidential interview space in Zone C.

variants.reordered: Many community leaders do not report incidents because they fear retaliation from survivors.
variants.paraphrase: The camp lacks any secure shelter of its own, and reaching the closest one takes four hours by road.

passages.source_passage: The town of Orlinsk and its surrounding villages have a population of about 120,000, yet there is not a single psychiatrist working in the district. Since the floods of 2022, local health workers have reported a sharp rise in sleep problems, grief and alcohol use. A household survey by the Clearwell Counselling Collective in 2023 found that 27 percent of adults showed signs of moderate or severe distress. Fewer than one in ten of those adults had spoken to anyone outside their family about it. Since 2020, our 14 lay counsellors have offered free group sessions in community halls. Demand now exceeds capacity, and clients wait up to six weeks for a first appointment. Counsellors are not paid for travel, which limits visits to remote villages.
